children: Shares of PC Jeweller rose up to 6 per cent on Thursday after the company said it had cleared and repaid all outstanding debt of nine out of its 14 consortium banks.
The stock hit an intraday high of Rs 10.75 per share on the NSE, up 5.6 per cent.
The stock snapped a two-day decline following the company's update.

In an exchange filing, the company said that, in line with its objective of becoming debt-free in the current month, it had successfully cleared and repaid all outstanding debt under the terms of the Settlement Agreement dated September 30, 2024, with respect to one more bank.

"With this successful clearance of debt, the Company has now repaid all the outstanding debt of 9 out of the 14 consortium banks with all repayments completed ahead of scheduled due dates. Further, the company has discharged more than 96% of the outstanding debt of the remaining 5 banks as well," it said.

"The company remains firmly on track to discharge the remaining less than 4% of the outstanding debt of the remaining 5 banks and achieve a debt-free status in the current month itself, which will materially strengthen its balance sheet and financial position," the company added.

title: PC Jeweller shares rise up to 6% as firm clears debt of 9 banks
